To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a resource allocation model for virtual cluster computing systems that provides a continuum of scheduling policies and that the model is useful for estimating the resource requirements for efficient and reliable virtual cluster computing.

we developed an analytical resource prediction framework for a virtual cluster computing system and that we demonstrated how the framework can be used to estimate the size and performance of the virtual cluster computing system.

(1) the resource allocation model is a good approximation of the resource allocation behavior of virtual cluster systems; (2) the resource prediction model provides an accurate estimate of the resources needed to provide a desired level of performance for a virtual cluster system; (3) the queue model provides an accurate approximation of the queue wait time; and (4) the spare resource model is a good predictor of the spare resource requirements for a reliable virtual cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of efficient and reliable virtual cluster computing.
the development of flexible and reliable virtual cluster systems for high performance cloud computing systems.
the problem of providing reliable and predictable virtual cluster computing systems using cloud computing resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we present a continuum model of scheduling policies that can be used to predict queue wait times for a virtual cluster computing system and that the results of the study show that it is feasible to provide a reliable, responsive, and cost-effective virtual high performance computing system.
the results of this research provide a foundation for future work in virtual cluster resource allocation and scheduling.

we have shown that it is possible, using our resource prediction model, to estimate the size and cost of a virtual cluster system needed for efficient, responsive, reliable, and predictable high performance computing services.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model that allows us to estimate the amount of resources required to provide a reliable and predictable grade of service to a virtual cluster system.
it is possible for cloud computing providers to provide reliable virtual cluster systems using a limited pool spare resources.
it is possible for a cloud computing provider to offer virtual high performance computing services to its customers by using spare resources to operate a reliable virtual cluster.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible for cloud computing providers to operate virtual cluster systems that provide a predictable and reliable grade of service.
the queue wait time and the resource allocation time for virtual cluster systems can be estimated and controlled by adjusting the resource allocation policy.
it is possible and practical to create virtual cluster systems that provide predictable levels of service and reliability.
